facts.text: A workstation is one powerful desktop computer; a cluster is many computers wired together and managed as one; high-performance computing (HPC) is the largest class of cluster, built for scientific calculation.
facts.quote: A workstation is one powerful desktop computer; a cluster is many computers wired together and managed as one; high-performance computing (HPC) is the largest class of cluster, built for scientific calculation.

facts.text: An engineer running one simulation at a time needs a workstation with a strong CPU, a capable GPU and a large disk.
facts.quote: One engineer running one simulation at a time needs a workstation: a desktop with a strong central processor (CPU), a capable graphics processing unit (GPU) and a large disk.

facts.text: CARLA alone requires 130 GB of disk space.
facts.quote: CARLA alone asks for 130 GB of disk space [Chapter 11].

facts.text: A program that must run thousands of scenarios in four months needs a cluster rather than queuing simulations one by one on desktops. The cluster uses tens or hundreds of rack-mounted computers and scheduling software to assign runs to free machines and gather results.
facts.quote: It needs a cluster: tens or hundreds of computers in racks, with scheduling software that hands each run to a free machine and gathers the results.

facts.text: A digital-twin off-road validation study used HPC clusters because sequential parameter sweeps could not explore the variability space within the time constraints.
facts.quote: A digital-twin off-road validation study ran on HPC clusters because sequential parameter sweeps could not explore the variability space under time constraints

facts.text: The group conducting the digital-twin off-road validation study ran 128 simulated off-road braking cases using HPC clusters.
facts.quote: the same group ran 128 simulated off-road braking cases this way.

facts.text: A radar signature calculation used eight supercomputer nodes with four GPUs per node.
facts.quote: A radar signature calculation used eight supercomputer nodes with four GPUs each.

facts.text: A European virtual-testing study needed more than 800 hours of compute.
facts.quote: A European virtual-testing study needed "800+ hours" of compute

facts.text: A European virtual-testing study needed more than 300 hours of manual case selection.
facts.quote: A European virtual-testing study needed "800+ hours" of compute and "300+ hours" of manual case selection [Chapters 1, 5, 6].

facts.text: In a four-month validation window, tests per wall-clock hour matter more than real-time rendering; low-fidelity models should screen the broad test space, and expensive models should run only where needed.
facts.quote: in a four-month window, tests per wall-clock hour matter more than real-time rendering: low-fidelity models should screen the broad space and expensive models should run only where they are needed [Chapter 5].

facts.text: The recommended compute architecture assigns logic tests to commodity servers or cloud containers, sensor tests to GPU workers, soil tests to dedicated GPU or HPC workers, and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing to a local real-time system.
facts.quote: commodity servers or cloud containers for logic tests, GPU workers for sensors, dedicated GPU or HPC workers for soil, and a local real-time system for hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing

facts.text: Simulation orchestration and storage create their own CPU and database load, which must be considered in the compute architecture.
facts.quote: orchestration and storage become their own CPU and database load [Chapter 11].
